kicker: A decision model that reads once

scenes.headline: How d3-turbo reads a photo once for many questions
scenes.sub: One attention mask, and the cache it makes possible
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Kedge! A decision model reads a photo and answers typed questions about it. This one reads the photo once, however many questions you ask.

scenes.text: In the full-attention layers the state no longer reads the question, so its hidden states are the same for every question and can be computed once.
scenes.mark: the state no longer reads the question
scenes.say: The idea: the state stops looking at the question. So it is the same for every question, and is computed once.

left.title: d3
left.say: In d3, the state reads the question, so every question pays for the photo again.

right.title: d3-turbo
right.say: In d3-turbo, the state reads only itself. The photo is read once.

steps.say: First, the photo and the text run through all sixty-four layers, once.
The runtime keeps the attention keys and values, and the final state of each linear scan.
Then the short question blocks run on top, each reading the cached state and itself.
A readout over answer codes gives every option a probability. No text is generated.

scenes.title: 255 questions about one photo
scenes.note: The vendor's timing on one MI325X
scenes.say: At two hundred fifty-five questions, the vendor times thirty-three seconds for the smaller d3-flash, and about two for d3-turbo.

scenes.title: Where is it? A Box answer
scenes.say: Box questions reuse the same readout.

items.say: Each edge is a distribution over one hundred twenty-eight steps.
Draw five hundred twelve boxes, and count how many overlap the answer.
A table turns that share into the confidence.

scenes.credit: d3-turbo model card, photo by Sally Wehner

steps.say: Four questions, four boxes, each with a confidence.
The camera gets low confidence. That is the confidence doing its job.

scenes.label: on the current text board, tied with d3
scenes.note: The #1 was the team's own estimate
scenes.say: Number one on both boards was the team's own estimate. On the official text board it is tenth, tied with d3.

scenes.text: The mask that keeps the state from reading the question is what makes reading it once legal.
scenes.say: Keep the state from reading the question, and you are allowed to read it once.

recap: The state never reads the question
Read once, cached, questions on top
Same accuracy as d3, far less waiting
scenes.say: Read once, cached, and the same accuracy as d3, with far less waiting.
